_comment: COUPLING tier-2, VECTOR, third backend pair. NGSolve and scikit-fem exchange a two-component displacement and a two-component traction across a straight interface, in both role/position arrangements, on interface meshes that do not match (NGSolve meshes with netgen, so its interface node count is whatever the mesher produces). NGSolve carries an API hazard the other backends do not: VectorH1 is blocked BY COMPONENT, so a vertex's u_x and u_y dofs are nv apart rather than adjacent — the opposite of dolfinx — and an adjacency assumption scatters u_y into the u_x block while leaving the array length, the solve and the convergence intact. Same componentwise assertions as vector_pair_fenics_skfem: both components alive and varying along the interface, continuity of u_x and u_y, equilibrium of t_x and t_y on the interface interior, per-component conservation, an empty `validation` block, and agreement with both the closed form and an un-split monolithic solve.

_mutation.note: The same one-wrong-material mutation as vector_pair_fenics_skfem: the LEFT participant gets a Poisson ratio 15% away from the one its boundary data and both references are built from. Convergence, displacement continuity and traction equilibrium all survive it — they are properties of the fixed point — while the interface state moves, because the two blocks' stiffness ratio changes in both components and the left block's prescribed y-face displacement stops being consistent with its own material. Only the closed-form and monolithic comparisons see it.
_mutation.from: x0, x1, e, nu = problem.xl, problem.xi, problem.el, problem.nul
_mutation.to: x0, x1, e, nu = problem.xl, problem.xi, problem.el, 1.15 * problem.nul
